attempts.summary: Configured VyOS on node1 (router between lan-a/node2 and lan-b/node3) with a default-drop forward filter that explicitly permits TCP/5432 from lan-a (10.60.1.0/24, node2) to lan-b (10.60.2.0/24, node3) plus established/related return traffic, and an explicit reject rule for all other inter-LAN traffic. Assigned static IPs/routes on node1 (eth1/eth2) and via NetworkManager on node2/node3 (enp8s0) after discovering NetworkManager was reconciling away manually-set IPs. Verified end-to-end with a real TCP listener (socat) on node3:5432: allowed traffic succeeds, ping and SSH between the LANs are actively rejected (ICMP port-unreachable / TCP refused). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming boot_id changes and full persistence/recovery of network config, VyOS firewall rules, and cross-LAN behavior after each reboot.
